articles.title_original: Spain announces ban on evictions after protests over 87-year-old woman's removal from flat
articles.title_zh: Spain announces ban on evictions after protests over 87-year-old woman's removal from flat
facts_zh:
Spain announces ban on evictions after protests over 87-year-old woman's removal from flat
- Published
Spain's coalition government has approved new housing measures following protests over the country's housing crisis, sparked by the eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her home in Madrid last week.
Ministers met on Tuesday to discuss the proposals, which include a ban on evictions until 2030.

Announcing the measures, Health Minister Mónica García said they would bring relief to more than five million people - but opposition politician Míriam Nogueras said the agreement left "small landlords out in the cold".

all_titles.en: Spain announces ban on evictions after protests over 87-year-old woman's removal from flat

articles.title_original: Trump rules out joint US-China venture to develop AI
articles.title_zh: Trump rules out joint US-China venture to develop AI
facts_zh:
Trump rules out joint US-China venture to develop AI
- Published
US President Donald Trump has ruled out any sort of joint venture with China in artificial intelligence (AI), arguing it would be tantamount to "giving away secrets" to America's main economic rival.
Speaking at an event in Washington on Tuesday, Trump again argued against putting any restrictions on the technology that would stifle growth in the future, despite mounting public concern.
Following Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to the White House last week, Beijing and Washington announced the launch of a new AI dialogue, with further talks scheduled for November.

all_titles.en: Trump rules out joint US-China venture to develop AI

articles.title_original: Dutch police arrest suspected member of group that claimed FBI hack
articles.title_zh: Dutch police arrest suspected member of group that claimed FBI hack
facts_zh:
Dutch police arrest suspected member of group that claimed FBI hack
- Published
Dutch police have arrested a suspected member of the ShinyHunters cyber-crime group that claimed to have stolen sensitive information on all FBI bureau staff - around 38,000 people.
After the alleged attack last week, the group claimed to have every agent's name, role, badge number and personal details including home address and phone numbers.
In a statement, Dutch police said it had arrested a 24-year-old man from Amsterdam on suspicion of being part of the group, which has also claimed other hacks.

all_titles.en: Dutch police arrest suspected member of group that claimed FBI hack

articles.title_original: Nigerian dances non-stop for seven days in world record bid
articles.title_zh: Nigerian dances non-stop for seven days in world record bid
facts_zh:
Nigerian dances non-stop for seven days in world record bid
- Published
A Nigerian dancer has completed a 168-hour dance marathon in Lagos in a bid to set a new world record.
Benjamin Daniel, known as "Ben Dancer", aimed to dance for seven days to break the Guinness World Records title for the longest dance marathon by an individual.

Cheered on by friends and supporters at Lagos's Freedom Park, the 33-year-old reached his target time at around 03:00 local time but continued dancing for another nine hours until midday, his team says.

all_titles.en: Nigerian dances non-stop for seven days in world record bid

articles.title_original: US prosecutors reopen case of alleged gang rape at Cornell University
articles.title_zh: US prosecutors reopen case of alleged gang rape at Cornell University
facts_zh:
US prosecutors reopen case of alleged gang rape at Cornell University
- Published
New York state prosecutors say they will reopen a criminal inquiry into the alleged rape of a woman at Cornell University in 2024.
The woman filed a civil lawsuit on 16 September alleging she was drugged and raped by multiple people at a fraternity house at the university.

"Once we determine the appropriate charges, the case will be prosecuted in the most objective and impartial means possible" through a grand jury, Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said Monday.

all_titles.en: US prosecutors reopen case of alleged gang rape at Cornell University

articles.title_original: US ban on Canadian alcohol and dairy takes effect as trade war drags on
articles.title_zh: US ban on Canadian alcohol and dairy takes effect as trade war drags on
facts_zh:
US ban on Canadian alcohol and dairy takes effect as trade war drags on
- Published
A US ban on several Canadian imports, including alcohol, dairy and motorcycles, has come into effect as a trade war between the two neighbours drags on.
The latest measure by the Trump administration is in response to Canada's implementation of tariffs on a range of US goods earlier this month following a breakdown in trade talks.
Canada is not expected to retaliate further, with Prime Minister Mark Carney saying earlier this month that the impact the import bans will have on Canada's economy is "modest".

all_titles.en: US ban on Canadian alcohol and dairy takes effect as trade war drags on

articles.title_original: Malaysia begins controversial repatriation of asylum seekers to Myanmar
articles.title_zh: Malaysia begins controversial repatriation of asylum seekers to Myanmar
facts_zh:
Malaysia begins controversial repatriation of asylum seekers to Myanmar
- Published
The Malaysian government has started repatriating around 5,000 asylum seekers from Myanmar, under a controversial deal agreed with Myanmar's military ruler Min Aung Hlaing.
Three ships from the Myanmar navy departed from Malaysia on Tuesday carrying the first 1,476 returnees.
Human rights groups have condemned the repatriation, saying the returnees could face violence, persecution and forced conscription into the Myanmar army.

all_titles.en: Malaysia begins controversial repatriation of asylum seekers to Myanmar

articles.title_original: Estonia blames Russia for arson at defence company supplying Ukraine
articles.title_zh: Estonia blames Russia for arson at defence company supplying Ukraine
facts_zh:
Estonia blames Russia for arson at defence company supplying Ukraine
- Published
Russia was behind an arson attack on an Estonian defence company in the capital Tallinn last month, authorities say.
Prime Minister Kristen Michal said the attack on Milrem Robotics - which supplies Ukraine with unmanned military vehicles - was ordered by Russian special services, but gave no details.
Moscow has been accused of launching sabotage attacks in a number of Nato countries that have been helping Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of its neighbour in February 2022.

all_titles.en: Estonia blames Russia for arson at defence company supplying Ukraine

articles.title_original: Hurricane Polo makes landfall on Mexico's Pacific coast
articles.title_zh: Hurricane Polo makes landfall on Mexico's Pacific coast
facts_zh:
Hurricane Polo makes landfall on Mexico's Pacific coast
- Published
Hurricane Polo has made landfall along the northern Pacific coast of Mexico, lashing the state of Baja California Sur with life-threatening winds and heavy rain that has already flooded some coastal areas.
Mexican officials said Polo moved ashore just south of the surfing and fishing village of Las Barrancas bringing maximum sustained winds of 110 mph (175 km/h).

Polo is moving northeast and on the forecast track, its core is predicted to continue passing over Baja California Sur before moving inland over the southern part of the Mexican state of Sonora later on Tuesday.

all_titles.en: Hurricane Polo makes landfall on Mexico's Pacific coast
